For non-virtualized callers, pass `0` or\n    /// use [`Self::row_attrs`].\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn row_attrs_indexed(&self, row_id: &Key, row_index: usize) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        let part = Part::Row { key: row_id.clone() };\n        set_part(&mut p, &part);\n        let selected = self.is_row_selected(row_id);\n        let expanded = self.is_row_expanded(row_id);\n        let disabled = self.is_row_disabled(row_id);\n        if self.ctx.selection_mode != selection::Mode::None {\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Selected), if selected { \"true\" } else { \"false\" });\n            if selected {\n                p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-selected\"), true);\n            }\n        }\n        if expanded {\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Expanded), \"true\");\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-expanded\"), true);\n        }\n        if disabled {\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), \"true\");\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-disabled\"), true);\n        }\n        if self.ctx.interactive {\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Role, \"row\");\n        }\n        if self.ctx.virtual_scrolling {\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::RowIndex), (row_index + 1).to_string());\n        }\n        p\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for a `<tr>` row using `row_index = 0`.\n    /// Convenience for non-virtualized tables.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn row_attrs(&self, row_id: &Key) -> AttrMap {\n        self.row_attrs_indexed(row_id, 0)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns row attributes for a row that acts as a link.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn row_link_attrs(&self, row_id: &Key, href: &str) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = self.row_attrs(row_id);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-href\"), href.to_owned());\n        p\n    }\n\n    // ── Headers / cells ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for a `<th scope=\"col\">` column header.\n    ///\n    /// Non-sortable columns omit `aria-sort` entirely per spec §3.4.2.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn column_header_attrs(&self, column: &str, sortable: bool) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        let part = Part::ColumnHeader { header: column.to_owned() };\n        set_part(&mut p, &part);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Scope, \"col\");\n        if sortable {\n            let is_sorted = self.active_sort_column().is_some_and(|c| c == column);\n            let aria_sort = if is_sorted {\n                match self.sort_direction() {\n                    Some(SortDirection::Ascending) => \"ascending\",\n                    Some(SortDirection::Descending) => \"descending\",\n                    None => \"none\",\n                }\n            } else {\n                \"none\"\n            };\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Sort), aria_sort);\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-sort\"), aria_sort);\n            if is_sorted {\n                p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-sorted\"), true);\n            }\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, \"0\");\n        }\n        p\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for a `<th scope=\"row\">` row header cell.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn row_header_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        set_part(&mut p, &Part::RowHeader);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Scope, \"row\");\n        p\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for a `<td>` cell.\n    ///\n    /// Manages a roving `tabindex` when the table is `interactive`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn cell_attrs(&self, col: usize, row: usize) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        let part = Part::Cell { col, row };\n        set_part(&mut p, &part);\n        if self.ctx.interactive {\n            let focused = self.ctx.focused_cell == Some((col, row));\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, if focused { \"0\" } else { \"-1\" });\n        }\n        p\n    }\n\n    // ── Selection controls ────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for the SelectAll checkbox.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an empty map when\n    /// [`SelectAllMode::None`](crate::data_display::table::SelectAllMode::None)\n    /// is configured.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn select_all_attrs(&self, all_row_ids: &[&Key]) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        if matches!(self.ctx.select_all_mode, SelectAllMode::None) {\n            return p;\n        }\n        set_part(&mut p, &Part::SelectAllCheckbox);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Type, \"checkbox\");\n        let count = match &self.ctx.select_all_mode {\n            SelectAllMode::AllData { total_count } => *total_count,\n            _ => all_row_ids.len(),\n        };\n        let label = (self.ctx.messages.select_all)(count, &self.ctx.locale);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label);\n        let all = self.all_selected(all_row_ids);\n        let some = !all && self.some_selected(all_row_ids);\n        let aria_checked = if all {\n            \"true\"\n        } else if some {\n            \"mixed\"\n        } else {\n            \"false\"\n        };\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Checked), aria_checked);\n        if all {\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Checked, true);\n        }\n        if some {\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-indeterminate\"), true);\n        }\n        p\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for the per-row selection checkbox.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn row_checkbox_attrs(&self, row_id: &Key) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        let part = Part::RowCheckbox { key: row_id.clone() };\n        set_part(&mut p, &part);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Type, \"checkbox\");\n        let selected = self.is_row_selected(row_id);\n        let label = (self.ctx.messages.select_row)(&self.ctx.locale);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Checked), if selected { \"true\" } else { \"false\" });\n        if selected {\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Checked, true);\n        }\n        if self.is_row_disabled(row_id) {\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), \"true\");\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true);\n        }\n        p\n    }\n\n    // ── Expand controls ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for an expand trigger `<button>`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn expand_trigger_attrs(&self, row_id: &Key) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        let part = Part::ExpandTrigger { key: row_id.clone() };\n        set_part(&mut p, &part);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Type, \"button\");\n        let expanded = self.is_row_expanded(row_id);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Expanded), if expanded { \"true\" } else { \"false\" });\n        let detail_id = format!(\"{}-expanded-{}\", self.ctx.id, row_id);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Controls), detail_id);\n        if expanded {\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-expanded\"), true);\n        }\n        if self.is_row_disabled(row_id) {\n            p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), \"true\");\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true);\n        }\n        p\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for the expanded detail `<tr>`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn expanded_content_attrs(&self, row_id: &Key) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        let detail_id = format!(\"{}-expanded-{}\", self.ctx.id, row_id);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Id, detail_id);\n        let part = Part::ExpandedContent { key: row_id.clone() };\n        set_part(&mut p, &part);\n        let expanded = self.is_row_expanded(row_id);\n        if expanded {\n ─────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Returns the attribute map for a column resize handle.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn column_resize_handle_attrs(&self, column: &str, current_width: f64) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut p = AttrMap::new();\n        let part = Part::ColumnResizeHandle { column: column.to_owned() };\n        set_part(&mut p, &part);\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Role, \"separator\");\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Orientation), \"vertical\");\n        let effective_width = self\n            .ctx\n            .column_widths\n            .get(column)\n            .copied()\n            .unwrap_or(current_width);\n        p.set(\n            HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueNow),\n            format_width(effective_width),\n        );\n        if self.ctx.resizing_column.as_deref() == Some(column) {\n            p.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-resizing\"), true);\n        }\n        p.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, \"0\");\n        p\n    }\n\n    // ── Keyboard navigation ───────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Handle a keydown event delivered to a row element. Emits the\n    /// appropriate [`Event::FocusRow`] / [`Event::ToggleRow`] /\n    /// [`Event::EscapeKey`] event.\n    pub fn on_row_keydown(&self, row_id: &Key, data: &KeyboardEventData, all_row_ids: &[&Key]) {\n        let current_idx = all_row_ids.iter().position(|id| *id == row_id);\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => {\n                if let Some(idx) = current_idx {\n                    if let Some(next) = all_row_ids.get(idx + 1) {\n                        (self.send)(Event::FocusRow((*next).clone()));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => {\n                if let Some(idx) = current_idx {\n                    if idx > 0 {\n                        if let Some(prev) = all_row_ids.get(idx - 1) {\n                            (self.send)(Event::FocusRow((*prev).clone()));\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Home => {\n                if let Some(first) = all_row_ids.first() {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusRow((*first).clone()));\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::End => {\n                if let Some(last) = all_row_ids.last() {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusRow((*last).clone()));\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Enter | KeyboardKey::Space => {\n                (self.send)(Event::ToggleRow(row_id.clone()));\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Escape => {\n                (self.send)(Event::EscapeKey);\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a keydown event delivered to a cell element when the table\n    /// is `interactive=true`. Resolves Arrow Left/Right against\n    /// [`Context::dir`] so Arrow Right always moves toward the logical\n    /// \"end\" column.\n    pub fn on_cell_keydown(\n        &self,\n        row_id: &Key,\n        col: usize,\n        data: &KeyboardEventData,\n        all_row_ids: &[&Key],\n        col_count: usize,\n    ) {\n        let current_row_idx = all_row_ids.iter().position(|id| *id == row_id);\n        let is_rtl = self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl;\n        let (next_col_key, prev_col_key) = if is_rtl {\n            (KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft, KeyboardKey::ArrowRight)\n        } else {\n            (KeyboardKey::ArrowRight, KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft)\n        };\n\n        match data.key {\n            k if k == next_col_key => {\n                if col + 1 < col_count {\n                    if let Some(idx) = current_row_idx {\n                        (self.send)(Event::FocusCell {\n                            row: row_id.clone(),\n                            col: col + 1,\n                            row_index: idx,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            k if k == prev_col_key => {\n                if col > 0 {\n                    if let Some(idx) = current_row_idx {\n                        (self.send)(Event::FocusCell {\n                            row: row_id.clone(),\n                            col: col - 1,\n                            row_index: idx,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => {\n                if let Some(idx) = current_row_idx {\n                    if let Some(next) = all_row_ids.get(idx + 1) {\n                        (self.send)(Event::FocusCell {\n                            row: (*next).clone(),\n                            col,\n                            row_index: idx + 1,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => {\n                if let Some(idx) = current_row_idx {\n                    if idx > 0 {\n                        if let Some(prev) = all_row_ids.get(idx - 1) {\n                            (self.send)(Event::FocusCell {\n                                row: (*prev).clone(),\n                                col,\n                                row_index: idx - 1,\n                            });\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Home if data.ctrl_key => {\n                if let Some(first) = all_row_ids.first() {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusCell {\n                        row: (*first).clone(),\n                        col: 0,\n                        row_index: 0,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::End if data.ctrl_key => {\n                if let Some(last) = all_row_ids.last() {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusCell {\n                        row: (*last).clone(),\n                        col: col_count.saturating_sub(1),\n                        row_index: all_row_ids.len().saturating_sub(1),\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Home => {\n                if let Some(idx) = current_row_idx {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusCell {\n                        row: row_id.clone(),\n                        col: 0,\n                        row_index: idx,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::End => {\n                if let Some(idx) = current_row_idx {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusCell {\n                        row: row_id.clone(),\n                        col: col_count.saturating_sub(1),\n                        row_index: idx,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Space => {\n                (self.send)(Event::ToggleRow(row_id.clone()));\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Escape => {\n                (self.send)(Event::EscapeKey);\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a keydown event delivered to a column resize handle.\n    /// Emits [`Event::ColumnResize`] with the current width adjusted by\n    /// [`Context::column_resize_step`], honoring RTL.\n    pub fn on_resize_handle_keydown(\n        &self,\n        column: &str,\n        current_width: f64,\n        data: &KeyboardEventData,\n    ) {\n        let step = self.ctx.column_resize_step;\n        let is_rtl = self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl;\n        let (grow_key, shrink_key) = if is_rtl {\n            (KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft, KeyboardKey::ArrowRight)\n        } else {\n            (KeyboardKey::ArrowRight, KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft)\n        };\n\n        let next_width = match data.key {\n            k if k == grow_key => Some(current_width + step),\n            k if k == shrink_key => Some(current_width - step),\n            _ => None,\n        };\n\n        if let Some(width) = next_width {\n            (self.send)(Event::ColumnResize {\n                column: column.to_owned(),\n                width,\n            });\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<'a> ConnectApi for Api<'a> {\n    type Part = Part;\n\n    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Self::Part) -> AttrMap {\n        match &part {\n            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(),\n            Part::Table => self.table_attrs(),\n            Part::Caption => self.caption_attrs(),\n            Part::Head => self.head_attrs(),\n            Part::Body => self.body_attrs(),\n            Part::Foot => self.foot_attrs(),\n            Part::Row { key } => self.row_attrs(key),\n            Part::ColumnHeader { header } => self.column_header_attrs(header, true),\n            Part::RowHeader => self.row_header_attrs(),\n            Part::Cell { col, row } => self.cell_attrs(*col, *row),\n            Part::SelectAllCheckbox => self.select_all_attrs(&[]),\n            Part::RowCheckbox { key } => self.row_checkbox_attrs(key),\n            Part::ExpandTrigger { key } => self.expand_trigger_attrs(key),\n            Part::ExpandedContent { key } => self.expanded_content_attrs(key),\n            Part::ColumnResizeHandle { column } => self.column_resize_handle_attrs(column, 0.0),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Internal helpers\n// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Sets the canonical `data-ars-scope` / `data-ars-part` attribute pair.\nfn set_part(p: &mut AttrMap, part: &Part) {\n    let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = part.data_attrs();\n    p.set(scope_attr, scope_val);\n    p.set(part_attr, part_val);\n}\n\n/// Renders an `aria-valuenow` width value to a clean string, trimming a\n/// trailing `.0` when the width is integer-valued.\nfn format_width(width: f64) -> String {\n    if width.fract() == 0.0 {\n        format!(\"{:.0}\", width)\n    } else {\n        format!(\"{width}\")\n    }\n}\n"

String: /// Removes disabled keys from a [`selection::Set`].
fn prune_selection_against(set: &selection::Set, disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>) -> selection::Set {
    match set {
        selection::Set::Empty | selection::Set::All => set.clone(),
        selection::Set::Single(key) => {
            if disabled.contains(key) {
                selection::Set::Empty
            } else {
                selection::Set::Single(key.clone())
            }
        }
        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => {
            let pruned: BTreeSet<Key> = keys.iter().filter(|k| !disabled.contains(k)).cloned().collect();
            match pruned.len() {
                0 => selection::Set::Empty,
                1 => selection::Set::Single(pruned.into_iter().next().unwrap()),
                _ => selection::Set::Multiple(pruned),
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Restricts a [`selection::Set`] to keys present in `rows`. `All` is
/// preserved (it logically expands to the registered set).
fn restrict_selection_to_rows(set: &selection::Set, rows: &[Key]) -> selection::Set {
    match set {
        selection::Set::Empty | selection::Set::All => set.clone(),
        selection::Set::Single(key) => {
            if rows.contains(key) {
                selection::Set::Single(key.clone())
            } else {
                selection::Set::Empty
            }
        }
        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => {
            let pruned: BTreeSet<Key> = keys.iter().filter(|k| rows.contains(k)).cloned().collect();
            match pruned.len() {
                0 => selection::Set::Empty,
                1 => selection::Set::Single(pruned.into_iter().next().unwrap()),
                _ => selection::Set::Multiple(pruned),
            }
        }
    }

//! Spec-conformance tests for ars-components.
//!
//! Each module asserts that a component's `Part` enum matches the
//! anatomy table declared in `spec/components/.../{component}.md` §3.
//! The test layer is intentionally tiny — it leans on the derive-generated
//! `Part::scope()`, `Part::all()`, and `Part::name()` to compare against a
//! hand-rolled allow-list of `(Part, expected-kebab-name)` pairs per
//! component.
//!
//! New components SHOULD add a sibling module here (or extend an existing
//! one) so any drift between the spec's declared parts and the impl is
//! caught at build time, not by a reviewer's eye.

//! Spec-conformance tests for `crates/ars-components/src/navigation/*`.
//!
//! Each test pulls the expected anatomy from the corresponding component
//! spec's §2 / §5 anatomy tables and asserts the impl's `Part` enum
//! matches the declared `(scope, part-name)` ordering.

use ars_collections::Key;
use ars_components::navigation::tabs;

use super::helper::assert_anatomy;

#[test]
fn tabs_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    // Spec references:
    // - `spec/components/navigation/tabs.md` §2 base anatomy table
    //   declares Root / List / Tab / Indicator / Panel.
    // - §5.4 anatomy addition declares the Closable variant's
    //   `tab-close-trigger` part.
    //
    // Workspace convention (see `tests/spec_conformance/helper.rs`)
    // requires the first variant to be `Root`. The remaining variants
    // are listed in spec §2 declaration order, with `TabCloseTrigger`
    // appended last because §5 layers it on top of the base anatomy.
    assert_anatomy(
        "tabs",
        &[
            (tabs::Part::Root, "root"),
            (tabs::Part::List, "list"),
            (
                tabs::Part::Tab {
                    tab_key: Key::default(),
                },
                "tab",
            ),
            (tabs::Part::TabIndicator, "tab-indicator"),
            (
                tabs::Part::Panel {
                    tab_key: Key::default(),
                    tab_label: None,
                },
                "panel",
            ),
            (
                tabs::Part::TabCloseTrigger {
                    tab_label: String::new(),
                },
                "tab-close-trigger",
            ),
        ],
    );

  * `column_widths` are all clamped to `min_column_width`.\n        #[test]\n        #[ignore = \"proptest — nightly extended-proptest job\"]\n        fn proptest_table_event_sequences_preserve_invariants(\n            props in arb_props(),\n            events in prop::collection::vec(arb_event(), 0..64),\n        ) {\n            let mut service = Service::<table::Machine>::new(\n                props,\n                &Env::default(),\n                &table::Messages::default(),\n            );\n\n            // Register a known row set so SetRows pruning isn't a side\n            // channel for selection invariants.\n            drop(service.send(table::Event::SetRows(vec![\n                Key::int(0),\n                Key::int(1),\n                Key::int(2),\n                Key::int(3),\n            ])));\n\n            for event in events {\n                drop(service.send(event));\n\n                let ctx = service.context();\n\n                prop_assert!(\n                    no_disabled_keys_in_selection(ctx.selected_rows.get(), &ctx.disabled_keys),\n                    \"selection contained disabled key: {:?} (disabled={:?})\",\n                    ctx.selected_rows.get(),\n                    ctx.disabled_keys,\n                );\n\n                prop_assert!(\n                    ctx.expanded_rows.get().is_disjoint(&ctx.disabled_keys),\n                    \"expansion contained disabled key: {:?} (disabled={:?})\",\n                    ctx.expanded_rows.get(),\n                    ctx.disabled_keys,\n                );\n\n                for (column, width) in &ctx.column_widths {\n                    prop_assert!(\n                        *width >= ctx.min_column_width,\n                        \"column {column:?} width {width} below min {}\",\n                        ctx.min_column_width,\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }"
}

565	/// Removes disabled keys from a [`selection::Set`].
566	fn prune_selection_against(set: &selection::Set, disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>) -> selection::Set {
567	    match set {
568	        selection::Set::Empty | selection::Set::All => set.clone(),
569	        selection::Set::Single(key) => {
570	            if disabled.contains(key) {
571	                selection::Set::Empty
572	            } else {
573	                selection::Set::Single(key.clone())
574	            }
575	        }
576	        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => {
577	            let pruned: BTreeSet<Key> = keys
578	                .iter()
579	                .filter(|k| !disabled.contains(k))
580	                .cloned()
581	                .collect();
582	            match pruned.len() {
583	                0 => selection::Set::Empty,
584	                1 => selection::Set::Single(pruned.into_iter().next().unwrap()),
585	                _ => selection::Set::Multiple(pruned),
586	            }
587	        }
588	        // `selection::Set` is `#[non_exhaustive]` — leave unknown future
589	        // variants untouched so we never silently corrupt them.
590	        _ => set.clone(),
591	    }
592	}

1161	### 2.2 Expandable Row Anatomy
1162	
1163	Tables may support expandable rows that reveal additional detail content:
1164	
1165	- **Expand Trigger**: Each expandable row includes a toggle button (typically a chevron icon) as the first cell or as an overlay on the row. The trigger receives `aria-expanded="true|false"` reflecting the current state. The trigger button MUST also set `aria-controls` pointing to the `id` of the detail row so assistive technology can navigate directly to the expanded content.
1166	- **Content Area**: Expanded content is rendered as a full-width `<td colspan="...">` (spanning all columns) inside a `<tr>` immediately below the parent row.
1167	- **Toggle Anatomy**: The expand/collapse control is a `<button>` element with `aria-label` describing the action (e.g., "Expand row" / "Collapse row"), managed via the `Messages` i18n struct.
1168	
1169	#### 2.2.1 Nesting Rules
1170	
1171	- **Single-level expansion only**: Expandable rows support one level of expansion. A row can expand to show detail content, but the detail content MUST NOT itself contain expandable rows. Nested expansion introduces unpredictable keyboard navigation and screen reader confusion.
1172	- **Hierarchical data**: For tree-structured or multi-level hierarchical data, use the `TreeView` component instead of nested table expansion. TreeView provides proper `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, and `aria-posinset` attributes for arbitrary nesting depth.
1173	- **Indentation Level**: Since expansion is single-level, `aria-level` attributes are not used on expandable rows. All data rows are at the same level; expanded content is supplementary detail, not a child row.
1174	
1175	## 3. Accessibility
1176	
1177	### 3.1 ARIA Roles, States, and Properties
1178	
1179	- **role="grid"** when `interactive=true`; **role="table"** otherwise.
1180	- Sortable `ColumnHeader`: `aria-sort="ascending|descending|none"`. Enter/Space toggles sort.
1181	- `Row`: `aria-selected` present only when `selection_mode != None`.
1182	- `Row` with expand: `aria-expanded="true|false"`.
1183	- `SelectAllCheckbox`: `aria-checked="mixed"` (indeterminate) when a subset of rows selected.
1184	
1185	**`aria-sort` and `aria-current` Semantics**
1186	
1187	- Sortable column headers MUST set `aria-sort` to one of: `"ascending"`, `"descending"`, or `"none"`.
1188	- Non-sortable column headers MUST omit `aria-sort` entirely so screen readers can distinguish sortable from non-sortable columns.
1189	- When sort state changes (user clicks a column header), announce the new sort state via `LiveAnnouncer` with `Politeness::Polite`: e.g., `"Sorted by Name, ascending"`. Use the `Messages.sort_ascending` / `Messages.sort_descending` message keys.
1190	
1191	**Pagination `aria-current`:**
1192	
1193	- When Table includes pagination controls, the active page button MUST set `aria-current="page"` to indicate the current page to screen readers.
1194	- Other page buttons MUST NOT have `aria-current` set (omit the attribute entirely, do not set to `"false"`).
1195	
1196	### 3.2 Keyboard Interaction
1197	
1198	Grid keyboard navigation (when `interactive=true`):
1199	
1200	| Key          | Action                                                                                   |
1201	| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1202	| `ArrowUp`    | Move focus to the cell above                                                             |
1203	| `ArrowDown`  | Move focus to the cell below                                                             |
1204	| `ArrowLeft`  | Move focus to the previous cell (wraps to previous row)                                  |
1205	| `ArrowRight` | Move focus to the next cell (wraps to next row)                                          |
1206	| `Home`       | Move focus to the first cell in the current row                                          |
1207	| `End`        | Move focus to the last cell in the current row                                           |
1208	| `Ctrl+Home`  | Move focus to the first cell in the first row                                            |
1209	| `Ctrl+End`   | Move focus to the last cell in the last row                                              |
1210	| `Enter`      | Activate the focused cell's primary interactive content                                  |
1211	| `F2`         | Enter edit mode for the focused cell (if editable)                                       |
1212	| `Escape`     | Exit edit mode, return focus to the cell                                                 |
1213	| `Space`      | Select/deselect the focused row (if selection enabled)                                   |
1214	| `Tab`        | Move focus to the next focusable element inside the cell; if none, move to the next cell |
1215	
1216	### 3.3 Focus Management
1217	
1218	- When `interactive=true`, the Table renders `role="grid"` and manages a roving `tabindex` across cells. The currently focused cell has `tabindex="0"`; all other cells have `tabindex="-1"`.
1219	- On initial focus (Tab into the grid), focus lands on the first cell of the first data row (or the last-focused cell if one was previously focused).
1220	- Arrow keys move focus between cells without wrapping out of the grid. `Home`/`End` wrap within the current row; `Ctrl+Home`/`Ctrl+End` move to the first/last cell of the first/last row.
1221	- When a cell contains interactive content (links, buttons, inputs), `Enter` activates it and `Escape` returns focus to the cell container.
1222	
1223	### 3.4 Screen Reader Announcements
1224	
1225	Sorting operations MUST be announced to assistive technology so screen reader users
1226	understand how the data is currently ordered.
1227	
1228	#### 3.4.1 `Messages` Sort Keys
1229	
1230	The `Messages` struct (passed via props or the i18n message bundle) includes the
1231	following sort-related keys:
1232	
1233	```rust
1234	/// Sort-related message keys within the Table's message bundle.
1235	/// All messages support ICU MessageFormat placeholders.
1236	pub struct SortMessages {
1237	    /// Announced when a column is sorted ascending.
1238	    /// Placeholder: `{column}` — the column's visible header text.
1239	    /// Default: "{column} sorted ascending"
1240	    pub sort_ascending: String,
1241	
1242	    /// Announced when a column is sorted descending.
1243	    /// Default: "{column} sorted descending"
1244	    pub sort_descending: String,
1245	
1246	    /// Announced when sort is removed from a column.
1247	    /// Default: "{column} sort removed"
1248	    pub sort_none: String,
1249	
1250	    /// Hint text for sortable column headers (used in `aria-roledescription`
1251	    /// or as a tooltip). Default: "activate to sort"
1252	    pub sortable_hint: String,
1253	
1254	    /// Announced when multi-column sort changes.
1255	    /// Placeholder: `{columns}` — comma-separated list of active sort columns
1256	    /// with their directions (e.g., "Name ascending, Date descending").
1257	    /// Default: "sorted by {columns}"
1258	    pub multi_sort_changed: String,
1259	}
1260	```
1261	
1262	#### 3.4.2 `aria-sort` Attribute
1263	
1264	Each sortable `<th>` element MUST carry the `aria-sort` attribute reflecting its current
1265	sort state:
1266	
1267	| Sort State | `aria-sort` Value |
1268	| ---------- | ----------------- |
1269	| Ascending  | `"ascending"`     |
1270	| Descending | `"descending"`    |
1271	| Unsorted   | `"none"`          |
1272	
1273	Non-sortable columns MUST NOT include `aria-sort`.
1274	
1275	#### 3.4.3 Live Region Announcement Timing
1276	
1277	When a sort operation completes (i.e., the data has been reordered and the DOM updated),
1278	the adapter MUST inject the appropriate message into an `aria-live="polite"` live region.
1279	The announcement fires immediately after the sort transition — no artificial delay.
1280	
1281	For single-column sort, the adapter uses `sort_ascending` or `sort_descending` with the
1282	column name substituted. When sort is removed, `sort_none` is used.
1283	
1284	For multi-column sort, the adapter uses `multi_sort_changed` with a formatted list of all
1285	active sort columns and their directions, ordered by sort priority (primary first).
1286	
1287	```rust,no_check
1288	/// Adapter-side helper. The agnostic core does not implement this — it
1289	/// belongs to the adapter that owns the live-region rendering. The
1290	/// signature matches `SortDescriptor<String>` from `ars_collections`
1291	/// (the agnostic core's sort descriptor uses `column: String`, not a
1292	/// `column_key` field).
1293	fn build_sort_announcement(
1294	    columns: &[ColumnDef],
1295	    sort_descriptors: &[SortDescriptor<String>],
1296	    messages: &Messages,
1297	    locale: &Locale,
1298	) -> String {
1299	    if sort_descriptors.is_empty() {
1300	        return String::new();
1301	    }
1302	
1303	    if sort_descriptors.len() == 1 {
1304	        let desc = &sort_descriptors[0];
1305	        return match desc.direction {
1306	            SortDirection::Ascending  => (messages.sort_ascending)(locale),
1307	            SortDirection::Descending => (messages.sort_descending)(locale),
1308	        };
1309	    }
1310	
1311	    // Multi-column: build a comma-separated list.
1312	    let parts: Vec<String> = sort_descriptors
1313	        .iter()
1314	        .map(|desc| {
1315	            let col_name = columns
1316	                .iter()
1317	                .find(|c| c.key == desc.column)
1318	                .map(|c| c.header_text.as_str())
1319	                .unwrap_or("");
1320	            let dir = match desc.direction {
1321	                SortDirection::Ascending  => "ascending",
1322	                SortDirection::Descending => "descending",
1323	            };
1324	            format!("{col_name} {dir}")
1325	        })
1326	        .collect();
1327	
1328	    format!("sorted by {}", parts.join(", "))
1329	}
1330	```
1331	
1332	### 3.5 Virtual Scrolling
1333	
1334	When the Table uses virtual scrolling (only rendering visible rows), the `<table>` element must include `aria-colcount` and `aria-rowcount` attributes reflecting the total column and row counts (not just visible ones). Each visible `<tr>` must include `aria-rowindex` indicating its 1-based position in the full dataset.
1335	
1336	```rust,no_check
1337	// In table_attrs() when virtual scrolling is enabled:
1338	if self.ctx.virtual_scrolling {
1339	    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::RowCount), self.ctx.total_rows.to_string());
1340	    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ColCount), self.ctx.total_cols.to_string());
1341	}
1342	
1343	// In row_attrs(index):
1344	if self.ctx.virtual_scrolling {
1345	    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::RowIndex), (index + 1).to_string());
1346	}
1347	```
1348	
1349	> **Virtualizer Integration**: For large datasets, Table integrates with `Virtualizer` from `ars-collections` (§1.6 of `06-collections.md`). When `virtualizer: Option<Virtualizer>` is set in the Table context, only visible rows are rendered. The adapter wires scroll position updates to the Virtualizer, which computes the visible row range. A `ScrollToRow(Key)` event is available to programmatically scroll a specific row into view.
```

1381	
1382	### 3.5 Virtual Scrolling
1383	
1384	When the Table uses virtual scrolling (only rendering visible rows), the `<table>` element must include `aria-colcount` and `aria-rowcount` attributes reflecting the total column and row counts (not just visible ones). Each visible `<tr>` must include `aria-rowindex` indicating its 1-based position in the full dataset.
1385	
1386	```rust,no_check
1387	// In table_attrs() when virtual scrolling is enabled:
1388	if self.ctx.virtual_scrolling {
1389	    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::RowCount), self.ctx.total_rows.to_string());
1390	    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ColCount), self.ctx.total_cols.to_string());
1391	}
1392	
1393	// In row_attrs(index):
1394	if self.ctx.virtual_scrolling {
1395	    attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::RowIndex), (index + 1).to_string());
1396	}
1397	```
1398	
1399	> **Virtualizer Integration**: For large datasets, Table integrates with `Virtualizer` from `ars-collections` (§1.6 of `06-collections.md`). When `virtualizer: Option<Virtualizer>` is set in the Table context, only visible rows are rendered. The adapter wires scroll position updates to the Virtualizer, which computes the visible row range. A `ScrollToRow(Key)` event is available to programmatically scroll a specific row into view.
1400	
1401	#### 3.5.1 IntersectionObserver for Table Virtual Scroll
1402	
1403	When Table uses virtual scrolling for large datasets, the virtualizer MUST integrate with `IntersectionObserver` as specified in `06-collections.md` section "IntersectionObserver for Lazy Rendering & Virtual Scroll".

1456	
1457	- **RTL layout**: In right-to-left locales the column order is visually reversed via CSS
1458	  `direction: rtl`. Sort direction indicators flip accordingly. The machine is RTL-agnostic;
1459	  the adapter applies `dir="rtl"` on the `Root` element based on the active locale.
1460	
1461	> **Drag and Drop Reorder**: When `dnd_enabled: true` is set, Table integrates with `DraggableCollection<T>` and `DroppableCollection<T>` from `06-collections.md` §7. Each row gains an optional `DragHandle` anatomy part, and `DropIndicator` parts appear between rows during drag. Fires `CollectionDndEvent::Reorder` on drop.
1462	
1463	### 4.3 Locale-Aware String Collation
1464	
1465	When Table sorts columns containing string data, sorting MUST use locale-aware collation rather than byte-order comparison. The `Collator` from `ars-i18n` (backed by ICU4X `Collator`) provides this capability.

1520	
1521	**Exclusion-set pattern** — The `selection::Set::All` variant from `ars_collections` natively
1522	supports the "select all with exclusions" pattern. When the user selects all via `AllData`
1523	and then deselects individual rows, `selection::State::deselect()` transitions from `All` to
1524	`Keys(complement)` using the full known key set. For async/paginated collections where the
1525	full key set is unknown, the adapter should track an exclusion set alongside `selection::Set::All`:
1526	
1527	```rust
1528	/// Extended selection tracking for server-paginated AllData tables.
1529	/// Wraps the canonical `selection::Set` with an exclusion list for rows
1530	/// deselected after a bulk select-all on an incompletely-loaded collection.
1531	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
1532	pub struct BulkSelection {
1533	    /// Row IDs explicitly deselected after a `selection::Set::All` selection.
1534	    /// Only meaningful when `selected_rows` is `selection::Set::All`.
1535	    pub excluded: BTreeSet<Key>,
1536	}

9	# Table — Leptos Adapter
10	
11	## 1. Purpose and Adapter Scope
12	
13	This spec maps the core [`Table`](../../components/data-display/table.md) contract onto a Leptos 0.8.x adapter. The adapter must preserve the table selection, expansion, sorting, and focus machine while making semantic host choice, sort announcements, sticky-header ownership, virtualization hooks, and load-more behavior explicit.
14	
15	## 2. Public Adapter API
16	
17	```rust,no_check
18	pub struct TableRenderCell(pub Callback<table::CellRenderCtx, AnyView>);
19	pub struct TableRenderExpandedRow(pub Callback<Key, AnyView>);
20	
21	#[component]
22	pub fn Table(
23	    #[prop(optional)] id: Option<String>,
24	    columns: StaticCollection<table::ColumnDef>,
25	    rows: StaticCollection<table::RowDef>,
26	    #[prop(optional, into)] selected_rows: Option<Signal<selection::Set>>,
27	    #[prop(optional, into)] expanded_rows: Option<Signal<BTreeSet<Key>>>,
28	    #[prop(optional, into)] sort_descriptor: Option<Signal<Option<SortDescriptor<String>>>>,
29	    #[prop(optional)] selection_mode: Option<selection::Mode>,
30	    #[prop(optional)] selection_behavior: Option<selection::Behavior>,
31	    #[prop(optional)] disabled_keys: Option<BTreeSet<Key>>,
32	    #[prop(optional)] disallow_empty_selection: bool,
33	    #[prop(optional)] interactive: bool,
34	    #[prop(optional)] sticky_header: bool,
35	    #[prop(optional)] loading: bool,
36	    #[prop(optional)] on_selection_change: Option<Callback<selection::Set>>,
37	    #[prop(optional)] on_sort_change: Option<Callback<Option<SortDescriptor<String>>>>,
38	    #[prop(optional)] on_row_action: Option<Callback<Key>>,
39	    #[prop(optional)] on_load_more: Option<Callback<()>>,
40	    render_cell: TableRenderCell,
41	    #[prop(optional)] render_expanded_row: Option<TableRenderExpandedRow>,
42	    #[prop(optional)] empty_state: Option<Children>,
43	) -> impl IntoView
44	```
45	
46	The adapter owns table scaffolding, `colgroup`, sticky-header mechanics, sort announcements, empty state, loading rows, and load-more observation. Consumers provide cell and optional expanded-row content through render callbacks only.
47	
48	## 3. Mapping to Core Component Contract
49	
50	- Props parity: full parity with adapter render slots and callbacks.
51	- Part parity: full parity for root table anatomy plus optional select-all, column-resize, empty-state, skeleton-row, and loading-sentinel structures.
52	- Traceability note: this spec promotes semantic `table` vs interactive `grid` rendering, live sort announcements, load-more wiring, virtualization hooks, row-link handling, and column-width ownership from the agnostic spec.
53	
54	## 4. Part Mapping
55	
56	| Core part / structure             | Required? | Adapter rendering target                      | Ownership     | Attr source                                   | Notes                                                              |
57	| --------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
58	| `Root` / `Table`                  | required  | `<table>` inside an optional scroll container | adapter-owned | `api.root_attrs()`                            | `role="table"` by default, `role="grid"` when `interactive=true`.  |
59	| `Caption`                         | optional  | `<caption>`                                   | adapter-owned | `api.caption_attrs()`                         | Stable descriptive text.                                           |
60	| `ColumnHeader` / header row       | repeated  | `<th>` inside `<thead>`                       | adapter-owned | `api.column_header_attrs(column)`             | Sort state and resize handles live here.                           |
61	| `Row`                             | repeated  | `<tr>`                                        | adapter-owned | `api.row_attrs(key)`                          | Selection, expansion, disabled, and link affordances are explicit. |
62	| `Cell`                            | repeated  | `<td>`                                        | adapter-owned | `api.cell_attrs(cell)`                        | Roving tabindex only in interactive mode.                          |
63	| `ExpandedRow`                     | optional  | `<tr>`                                        | adapter-owned | adapter-local attrs plus core expansion state | Rendered after its owning row.                                     |
64	| `SelectAll`                       | optional  | `<input>` or adapter-owned control            | adapter-owned | `api.select_all_attrs()`                      | Only in multiple selection mode.                                   |
65	| `ColumnResizeHandle`              | optional  | `<div>`                                       | adapter-owned | `api.column_resize_handle_attrs(column)`      | Only when resizing is enabled.                                     |
66	| `EmptyState`                      | optional  | adapter-owned row or wrapper                  | adapter-owned | adapter-local attrs                           | Rendered when there are no rows.                                   |
67	| `SkeletonRow` / `LoadingSentinel` | optional  | adapter-owned rows or sentinel div            | adapter-owned | adapter-local attrs                           | Adapter concerns for loading and infinite scroll.                  |
68	
69	## 5. Attr Merge and Ownership Rules
70	
71	- Core attrs include row selection, expansion, sort, disabled, focus, and resize state.
72	- The adapter owns table vs grid semantics, `colgroup` widths, sticky-header styles, live-sort-region wiring, and row-link affordances.
73	- Consumer decoration must not replace `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, or `<td>` hosts or remove required ARIA and data attrs.
74	- Column widths are adapter-owned once resizing or sticky-header alignment is active.
75

[package]
name                   = "ars-components"
version                = "0.1.0"
edition.workspace      = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace      = true
description            = "Framework-agnostic component machines for ars-ui"
repository.workspace   = true

[features]
default = ["std"]
std = [
  "ars-collections/std",
  "ars-core/std",
  "ars-forms/std",
  "ars-i18n/std",
  "ars-interactions/std"
]
debug = ["dep:log", "ars-core/debug", "ars-interactions/debug"]
# Enables ICU4X-backed locale-aware Unicode case mapping (via
# `ars-i18n/icu4x`) and unlocks components whose spec contract requires it
# — currently `utility::highlight`. Adapters that want the browser
# `Intl` backend instead can build with `--no-default-features --features
# std,ars-i18n/web-intl`; in that combination, modules gated on `i18n`
# (Highlight) are not available.
i18n = ["ars-i18n/icu4x"]
uuid = ["ars-collections/uuid"]

[dependencies]
ars-a11y         = { path = "../ars-a11y", default-features = false }
ars-collections  = { path = "../ars-collections", default-features = false }
ars-core         = { path = "../ars-core", default-features = false }
ars-forms        = { path = "../ars-forms", default-features = false }
ars-i18n         = { path = "../ars-i18n", default-features = false }
ars-interactions = { path = "../ars-interactions", default-features = false }
log              = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
insta    = { version = "1", features = ["yaml"] }
proptest = "1"

[lints]
workspace = true

## Summary

Task **#286 — Implement Table agnostic core** is complete. Per CLAUDE.md step 8, presenting for review before any commit.

### Files modified
- `crates/ars-components/src/data_display/mod.rs` — `pub mod table;`
- `crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance.rs` — register `data_display`
- `crates/ars-components/tests/proptest_state_machines/data_display.rs` — `proptest_table_event_sequences_preserve_invariants`
- `spec/components/data-display/table.md` — drift fixes #1–#11 (see below)
- `spec/leptos-components/data-display/table.md` — corrected attr-source signatures
- `spec/dioxus-components/data-display/table.md` — corrected attr-source signatures

### Spec drifts fixed in the same PR
1. **§1.1.1** removed misleading `Scrolling` state mention
2. **§1.2** added `FocusRow`, `FocusCell { row, col, row_index }`, `EscapeKey`, `SetRows`, `SetDirection`, `SetRowCounts`, `SetLoading`, `ColumnResize{,End}`, `SyncProps`, `SyncControlled{SelectedRows,ExpandedRows,SortDescriptor}` to the Events table
3. **§1.3** added missing Context fields (`dir`, `is_sorting`, `rows`, `column_widths`, `resizing_column`, `virtual_scrolling`, `total_rows`, `total_cols`, `loading`, `escape_key_behavior`, `select_all_mode`, `min_column_width`, `column_resize_step`, `disallow_empty_selection`, `sticky_header`)
4. **§1.5** added `SelectAllMode` enum, new Props for variants
5. **§1.7** init now seeds `selection_state.selected_keys`, prunes disabled rows, resolves `Direction::Auto` from locale
6. **§1.7** transitions for `DeselectRow`/`DeselectAll`/`ToggleRow` now honor `disallow_empty_selection`; `EscapeKey` arm added; `ExpandRow` rejects disabled rows; `CollapseRow` is idempotent
7. **§1.7** fixed `Event::FocusCell` row-index bug (was hard-coding row 0)
8. **§1.8** added `column_resize_handle_attrs` and `on_resize_handle_keydown`
9. **§3.4.2** corrected "Non-sortable columns MUST omit `aria-sort`" wording
10. **§3.4.3** rewrote `build_sort_announcement` to compile against the real `SortDescriptor<String>` API (marked `rust,no_check`)
11. **§5.2** `BulkSelection::effective_count` made forward-compatible with `selection::Set`'s `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute

### Test counts

- **Spec-conformance**: 1 (anatomy match)
- **Proptest**: 1 (event-sequence invariants, ignored by default — runs on nightly extended-proptest)

### Decisions worth flagging
- **`type Effect = NoEffect`** — every Table transition is `context_only(...)`. Adapters read `ctx.focused_cell` / `ctx.focused_row` / `ctx.focused_col` directly to apply DOM focus, mirroring the spec's "live focus belongs in the adapter" rule. Adding `ScrollToRow(Key)` later will require widening `Effect` to a typed enum — this is the only known item explicitly deferred.
- **`selection::State::toggle` requires a `Collection` generic** — the Table machine doesn't own a `Collection`, so transitions compute toggle locally via `is_selected` + `select`/`deselect`.
- **`SyncControlledSortDescriptor(Option<SortDescriptor<String>>)`** wraps the payload in `Some(...)` inside the transition because the outer `Option` on `Bindable::sync_controlled` is the controlled-mode toggle, not the value itself.

The issue is on **In Progress** on the GitHub Project board. **No commit has been made yet** — awaiting your review before invoking `commit-push-pr` / `waiting-for-codex-review`.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply new props when handling SyncProps**

`Event::SyncProps` currently clones `ctx.disabled_keys` and only re-prunes existing state, but it never copies updated values from `props` into `Context` (e.g. `disabled_keys`, `selection_mode`, `interactive`, `sticky_header`, `virtual_scrolling`, resize settings). When props change, dispatching `SyncProps` cannot actually synchronize those fields, so row disabled state/ARIA behavior and interaction mode can remain stale relative to the latest props.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Materialize Set::All before toggling selected rows**

`ToggleRow` calls `toggle_state_without_collection`, which in the selected path delegates to `state.deselect(&key)`. For `selection::Set::All`, `deselect` is a no-op, so after `SelectAll` users cannot deselect an individual row via row toggle/checkbox. The helper comment says the caller should pre-handle `All`, but this call site does not, so selection gets stuck at `All` for per-row deselection.

This machine defines `SyncProps`, `SyncControlled*`, and `SetDirection` events, but it never overrides `Machine::on_props_changed`. `Service::set_props` only enqueues events returned by that hook, so runtime prop updates won't be mirrored into context/bindables, leaving controlled selection/sort/expansion and direction-dependent behavior stale after parent prop changes.

`SortColumn` unconditionally sets `ctx.is_sorting = true`, but this flag is only reset in `SyncControlledSortDescriptor`. In the default uncontrolled sort path, that sync event is not emitted, so one sort can leave `is_sorting` stuck `true` and any sort-loading indicator permanently active.

`select_all_attrs` only checks `select_all_mode` and still emits a live select-all checkbox when `selection_mode` is `Single` or `None`. In those modes `Event::SelectAll` is rejected, so the UI can expose a control that appears actionable but cannot work. This should be suppressed (empty attrs) unless `selection_mode == Multiple`.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Respect AllVisible semantics in SelectAll transition**

`Event::SelectAll` always calls `selection_state.select_all()` and writes `selection::Set::All` regardless of `select_all_mode`. In the default `AllVisible` mode this incorrectly selects rows that are not currently rendered (and even rows loaded later), because `Set::All` makes `is_row_selected` true for any key. The transition should only use global `All` for `AllData`; `AllVisible` should materialize the current row set.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle DeselectRow when selection is Set::All**

`DeselectRow` delegates to `selection_state.deselect(&key)`, but `deselect` is a no-op for `selection::Set::All`. That means per-row deselection fails after a bulk select-all when adapters emit `DeselectRow` directly (e.g., checkbox uncheck path), leaving every row selected. This path needs the same `All` materialization/exclusion handling as toggle.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebase focused_cell row index after SetRows reorder**

`SetRows` only clears focus when the focused row key disappears, but it never updates `focused_cell` when that same row remains and moves to a different index. After sorting/filtering/reorder updates, `focused_cell` can point at a stale row index while `focused_row` points at a different row, causing adapter focus wiring to target the wrong cell.

    fn on_props_changed(old: &Self::Props, new: &Self::Props) -> Vec<Self::Event> {
        let mut events = Vec::new();

        // `dir` is handled by `SetDirection`, not `SyncProps`. This split
        // lets the adapter resolve `Direction::Auto` once at mount via
        // `SetDirection(Rtl|Ltr)` and have that resolution survive
        // unrelated prop updates (e.g. `disabled_keys` deltas) — `SyncProps`
        // no longer rewrites `ctx.dir`. Conversely, an explicit
        // consumer-driven prop change to `dir` (including `Concrete →
        // Auto`, which signals "please re-resolve") propagates exactly
        // once through `SetDirection`. `SetDirection` itself is idempotent
        // when the new value already matches `ctx.dir`, so we can emit
        // unconditionally on prop deltas without thrashing.
        if old.dir != new.dir {
            events.push(Event::SetDirection(new.dir));
        }

        if non_dir_context_props_changed(old, new) {
            events.push(Event::SyncProps);
        }

        // The controlled-`value` Bindable is reflected into [`Context::value`]
        // via `Bindable::sync_controlled`. Detecting the prop delta here and
        // emitting [`Event::SyncControlledValue`] is the only path the agnostic
        // core offers for adapters to push controlled-value updates into
        // `Context` (the Bindable lives behind `&mut Context`, which only a
        // transition plan can mutate).
        if let (Some(old_value), Some(new_value)) = (&old.value, &new.value)
            && old_value != new_value
        {
            events.push(Event::SyncControlledValue(new_value.clone()));

/// responsibility); `dir` changes flow through [`Event::SetDirection`].
fn non_dir_context_props_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> bool {
    old.orientation != new.orientation
        || old.activation_mode != new.activation_mode
        || old.loop_focus != new.loop_focus
        || old.disabled_keys != new.disabled_keys
}

// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Transition helpers
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum FocusStep {
    Next,
    Prev,
}

/// Returns `true` when `tab` is in the disabled-tab set.
fn is_disabled(ctx: &Context, tab: &Key) -> bool {
    ctx.disabled_tabs.contains(tab)
}

The Table machine intentionally does\n/// not own a `Collection`, so it computes toggle directly from the\n/// `selection::Set::All` case.\nfn toggle_state_without_collection(state: &selection::State, key: Key) -> selection::State {\n    if state.is_disabled(&key) {\n        return state.clone();\n    }\n\n    if state.is_selected(&key) {\n        // `selection::State::deselect_from_all` requires a Collection;\n        // expand `All` to `Multiple(rows \\ {key})` below by caller —\n        // here we simply call `deselect` which handles `Set::All` by\n        // returning the state unchanged. The caller pre-handles `All`.\n        state.deselect(&key)\n    } else {\n        state.select(key)\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Materializes [`selection::Set::All`] against the registered row set\n/// so that `selection::State::deselect` (which is a no-op on `Set::All`)\n/// can subsequently drop individual keys. Used by [`Event::ToggleRow`]\n/// and [`Event::DeselectRow`] to keep individual-deselect workable after\n/// a bulk select-all.\nfn materialize_all_against_rows(state: &selection::State, rows: &[Key]) -> selection::State {\n    if !matches!(state.selected_keys, selection::Set::All) {\n        return state.clone();\n    }\n    let materialized: BTreeSet<Key> = rows\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|k| !state.is_disabled(k))\n        .cloned()\n        .collect();\n    let new_keys = match materialized.len() {\n        0 => selection::Set::Empty,\n        1 => selection::Set::Single(materialized.into_iter().next().unwrap()),\n        _ => selection::Set::Multiple(materialized),\n    };\n    selection::State {\n        selected_keys: new_keys,\n        ..state.clone()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Toggle helper that avoids the `Collection` generic on\n/// [`selection::State::toggle`]. The Table machine intentionally does\n/// not own a `Collection`, so it computes toggle directly. Callers\n/// pre-materialize [`selection::Set::All`] via\n/// [`materialize_all_against_rows`] so `deselect` can drop individual\n/// keys.\nfn toggle_state_without_collection(state: &selection::State, key: Key) -> selection::State {\n    if state.is_disabled(&key) {\n        return state.clone();\n    }\n\n    if state.is_selected(&key) {\n        state.deselect(&key)\n    } else {\n        state.select(key)\n    }\n}"

  "new_string": "    fn connect<'a>(\n        state: &'a Self::State,\n        ctx: &'a Self::Context,\n        props: &'a Self::Props,\n        send: &'a dyn Fn(Self::Event),\n    ) -> Self::Api<'a> {\n        Api {\n            state,\n            ctx,\n            props,\n            send,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn on_props_changed(old: &Self::Props, new: &Self::Props) -> Vec<Self::Event> {\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // `dir` flows through `SetDirection`, not `SyncProps`, so a\n        // runtime-resolved direction (e.g. one the adapter installed via\n        // `SetDirection` after resolving `Direction::Auto`) is not\n        // overwritten by an unrelated prop delta. `SetDirection` is\n        // idempotent.\n        if old.dir != new.dir {\n            events.push(Event::SetDirection(new.dir));\n        }\n\n        if non_dir_context_props_changed(old, new) {\n            events.push(Event::SyncProps);\n        }\n\n        // Each controlled Bindable has its own sync event because the\n        // outer `Option` is the controlled-mode toggle and the inner\n        // value carries the new content.\n        if old.selected_rows != new.selected_rows {\n            events.push(Event::SyncControlledSelectedRows(new.selected_rows.clone()));\n        }\n        if old.expanded_rows != new.expanded_rows {\n            events.push(Event::SyncControlledExpandedRows(new.expanded_rows.clone()));\n        }\n        if old.sort_descriptor.is_controlled()\n            && old.sort_descriptor.get() != new.sort_descriptor.get()\n        {\n            events.push(Event::SyncControlledSortDescriptor(\n                new.sort_descriptor.get().clone(),\n            ));\n        }\n\n        events\n    }\n}\n\n/// Returns `true` when any non-Bindable, non-direction Props field\n/// changed between renders. Drives the [`Event::SyncProps`] dispatch\n/// inside [`Machine::on_props_changed`].\nfn non_dir_context_props_changed(old: &Props, new: &Props) -> bool {\n    old.selection_mode != new.selection_mode\n        || old.selection_behavior != new.selection_behavior\n        || old.disabled_keys != new.disabled_keys\n        || old.disallow_empty_selection != new.disallow_empty_selection\n        || old.escape_key_behavior != new.escape_key_behavior\n        || old.select_all_mode != new.select_all_mode\n        || old.interactive != new.interactive\n        || old.sticky_header != new.sticky_header\n        || old.min_column_width.to_bits() != new.min_column_width.to_bits()\n        || old.column_resize_step.to_bits() != new.column_resize_step.to_bits()\n        || old.virtual_scrolling != new.virtual_scrolling\n        || old.total_rows != new.total_rows\n        || old.total_cols != new.total_cols\n}"
}

  "new_string": "#[test]\nfn table_sync_controlled_sort_descriptor_pushes_value() {\n    // `SyncControlledSortDescriptor` mirrors a parent-driven controlled\n    // value into the Bindable. `is_sorting` is no longer coupled to the\n    // sort transition — adapters drive it explicitly via `SetIsSorting`.\n    let mut service = service_with_rows(\n        Props {\n            sort_descriptor: Bindable::controlled(None),\n            ..test_props()\n        },\n        &[],\n    );\n    assert!(service.context().sort_descriptor.get().is_none());\n\n    drop(\n        service.send(Event::SyncControlledSortDescriptor(Some(SortDescriptor {\n            column: \"name\".to_string(),\n            direction: SortDirection::Ascending,\n        }))),\n    );\n\n    let descriptor = service.context().sort_descriptor.get().clone();\n    assert_eq!(\n        descriptor.as_ref().map(|d| d.column.as_str()),\n        Some(\"name\"),\n    );\n}"
}

Individual checkbox uncheck after a\n  bulk SelectAll now works.\n- `Machine::on_props_changed` is overridden to enqueue `SetDirection`,\n  `SyncProps`, `SyncControlledSelectedRows`, `SyncControlledExpandedRows`,\n  and `SyncControlledSortDescriptor` whenever the matching `Props`\n  field differs between renders. Runtime prop updates now propagate.\n- `Event::SelectAll` respects `SelectAllMode`:\n  * `AllData { .. }` writes `Set::All` (with `BulkSelection` exclusion\n    tracking from §5.2).\n  * `AllVisible` (default) materializes `Multiple(ctx.rows)` so unloaded\n    rows aren't falsely reported as selected.\n  * `None` rejects the event.\n\nP2 fixes:\n- `is_sorting` is now adapter-controlled via a new\n  `Event::SetIsSorting(bool)` event. The agnostic core no longer flips\n  the flag inside `SortColumn` — synchronous sorts complete in the same\n  render frame so the indicator would never be visible, and the\n  previous behavior left the flag stuck `true` in the uncontrolled\n  path. Async-sort adapters dispatch `SetIsSorting(true)` before the\n  reorder and `SetIsSorting(false)` when complete.\n- `select_all_attrs` now gates on `selection_mode == Multiple` in\n  addition to `SelectAllMode::None`. Single / None modes return an\n  empty `AttrMap` so adapters don't render an actionable checkbox the\n  machine will silently reject.\n- `Event::SetRows` now rebases `focused_cell.1` (row index) when the\n  focused row remains in the new row list but moves to a different\n  position (sort / filter / reorder). Two pre-existing\ntests updated to match the new is_sorting contract.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Dispatch sort sync when Bindable control mode changes**

`on_props_changed` only emits `SyncControlledSortDescriptor` when the *old* sort bindable is already controlled, so switching from `Bindable::uncontrolled(...)` to `Bindable::controlled(...)` is ignored. In that transition the context keeps using its local sort value and subsequent `SortColumn` updates can diverge from the parent-controlled prop, which breaks controlled-sort semantics until remount.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DSWzd ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1355
parent: 3269464327
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow sort descriptor to exit controlled mode**

The sync transition always calls `sync_controlled(Some(value))`, so the sort bindable can never be switched back to uncontrolled mode. If a parent changes from controlled to uncontrolled props, the table remains controlled with the last pushed value, causing stale sort ownership and preventing expected uncontrolled behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DSWzg ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1377
parent: 3269464332
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce stable component id on prop updates**

`on_props_changed` does not guard against `Props.id` changes, but `Context.id`/`caption_id` are only derived once in `init` and never resynced. If a caller updates props with a different id, `table_attrs`, `caption_attrs`, and expanded-row `aria-controls` ids remain stale, causing broken DOM id/ARIA linkage that is hard to diagnose.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DSWzi ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:2227
parent: 3269464339
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive SelectAll part attrs from registered rows**

`ConnectApi::part_attrs` routes `Part::SelectAllCheckbox` through `select_all_attrs(&[])`, so it always computes checked/mixed state against an empty row set. That makes the generic part API report incorrect `aria-checked`/indeterminate state whenever rows are selected, despite `Context::rows` already tracking the registered row ids.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DSWzm ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1395
parent: 3269464344
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync controlled loading bindable on props changes**

The comment says each controlled `Bindable` gets a dedicated sync event, but `loading: Bindable<bool>` is omitted from `on_props_changed`. As a result, `Service::set_props` updates to controlled loading state are never propagated to `Context.loading`, so loading indicators can remain stale unless adapters dispatch `SetLoading` manually.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DSWzs ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1325
parent: 3269464351
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply pruning to controlled selection and expansion**

`SyncProps` computes pruned selection/expansion but writes them with `set(...)`; for controlled bindables, `get()` still returns the external controlled value, so disabled or stale keys are not actually removed from API-visible state. This violates the documented pruning behavior when disabled keys or row registry constraints change.

bindable_sync_payload(&new.sort_descriptor),\n            ));\n        }\n        if bindable_controlled_state_changed(&old.loading, &new.loading) {\n            events.push(Event::SyncControlledLoading(bindable_sync_payload(\n                &new.loading,\n            )));\n        }\n\n        events\n    }\n}\n\n/// Detects any controlled-mode delta between two Bindables that warrants\n/// a sync event:\n///\n/// * Both controlled, values differ.\n/// * One side controlled, the other not.\nfn bindable_controlled_state_changed<T>(\n    old: &Bindable<T>,\n    new: &Bindable<T>,\n) -> bool\nwhere\n    T: ars_core::BindableValue,\n{\n    if old.is_controlled() != new.is_controlled() {\n        return true;\n    }\n    if new.is_controlled() && old.get() != new.get() {\n        return true;\n    }\n    false\n}\n\n/// Translates a Bindable into the `Option<T>` payload expected by\n/// [`Bindable::sync_controlled`]: `Some(value)` to enter/update\n/// controlled mode, `None` to exit.\nfn bindable_sync_payload<T>(b: &Bindable<T>) -> Option<T>\nwhere\n    T: ars_core::BindableValue,\n{\n    if b.is_controlled() {\n        Some(b.get().clone())\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}"
}

The same logic applies to\n  `loading` via the new `SyncControlledLoading` event.\n- `Event::SyncControlledSortDescriptor` payload widened to\n  `Option<Option<SortDescriptor<String>>>`. The outer `Option` is now\n  the controlled-mode toggle (`Some(opt)` enters controlled mode with\n  inner value `opt`; `None` exits controlled mode entirely), matching\n  `Bindable::sync_controlled`'s `Option<T>` semantics. Previously the\n  Bindable could never go back to uncontrolled.\n- New `Event::SyncControlledLoading(Option<bool>)` mirrors the\n  same outer-Option semantics for the loading Bindable, plus a\n  dispatch from `on_props_changed` so parent-controlled loading state\n  actually reaches Context.\n- `SyncProps` no longer corrupts controlled selection/expansion. For\n  controlled Bindables, `set()` only updates the internal value while\n  `get()` keeps returning the external value, so the previous pruning\n  write silently desynced `selection_state.selected_keys` from the\n  user-visible selection. The fix: only call `set()` when the Bindable\n  is uncontrolled, and always re-sync `selection_state.selected_keys`\n  from `selected_rows.get()` so the state machine and the API agree on\n  the current selection regardless of controlled-mode.\n\nP2 fixes:\n- `SyncProps` now rebuilds `Context.id` and `Context.caption_id` from\n  `ComponentIds::from_id(&new_props.id)` when `Props.id` changes, so\n  `table_attrs` / `caption_attrs` / `expand_trigger`-derived\n  `aria-controls` ids no longer go stale after a parent rename.\n  `non_dir_context_props_changed` now includes `id` in the delta check\n  so `SyncProps` actually fires on id changes.\n- `ConnectApi::part_attrs(Part::SelectAllCheckbox)` now routes through\n  `ctx.rows` instead of an empty slice. The dispatcher path no longer\n  incorrectly reports `aria-checked=false` when every registered row\n  is selected.\n\nTests: +7 new regression guards (TDD red → green) covering every\nfinding. Coverage on the table file went from 89.58% / 87.95%\n(line/branch) up to 92.74% / 91.40%.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep selection_state aligned with controlled selection in SetRows**

`SetRows` always assigns `ctx.selection_state.selected_keys = restricted_selection` even when `selected_rows` is controlled. In controlled mode, `ctx.selected_rows.set(...)` only updates the internal fallback, while `ctx.selected_rows.get()` still returns the parent value, so this creates a split brain: API reads report one selection set while transition guards (`selection_state`) use another after row-list updates (e.g., filtering/removing a selected row). That can make toggles/deselect guards behave inconsistently with what the UI reports as selected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DSv8M ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1380
parent: 3269605826
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resync selection_state when leaving controlled selected_rows**

`SyncControlledSelectedRows` only updates `selection_state.selected_keys` in the `Some(set)` branch. When props switch from controlled to uncontrolled (`None`), `sync_controlled(None)` changes what `selected_rows.get()` returns, but `selection_state.selected_keys` is left unchanged. If the internal fallback differs from the last controlled value, selection checks and transition logic diverge immediately after the mode switch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
```

    /// The component reads the controlled value via [`get`](Self::get).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn controlled(value: T) -> Self {
        Self {

    /// Creates an uncontrolled bindable managed by the component.

    #[must_use]
    pub const fn uncontrolled(default: T) -> Self {

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve AllData semantics when deselecting one row**

When `SelectAllMode::AllData` has put selection into `Set::All`, this helper rewrites that state to only the currently registered `rows`. The first `DeselectRow`/`ToggleRow` therefore drops every unloaded row from selection, so subsequent bulk actions target only visible rows instead of the full dataset. For paginated/async tables this is a correctness break; `Set::All` needs to stay global with exclusions tracked separately.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTElY ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:2121
parent: 3269730134
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip disabled rows during arrow-key focus movement**

Arrow navigation picks the next/previous entry from `all_row_ids` without checking whether that row is disabled. In interactive tables that include disabled rows, this emits `FocusRow` for `aria-disabled` rows and adapters will move DOM focus onto elements that are meant to be non-interactive. Navigation should ignore disabled targets (or focus events should reject disabled keys) to keep disabled-row behavior consistent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTElb ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:2209
parent: 3269730138
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent cell arrow keys from focusing disabled rows**

Cell navigation uses `all_row_ids` directly and sends `FocusCell` for the adjacent row without filtering out disabled keys. With a disabled row between enabled rows, pressing `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` moves logical focus onto the disabled row, contradicting the component’s non-interactive disabled-row contract and causing adapters to target a row that should not receive interaction focus.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTEld ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1686
parent: 3269730141
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expose multi-select capability on interactive grid**

When `interactive=true` and row selection allows multiple rows, rows emit `aria-selected` but the grid root never sets `aria-multiselectable="true"`. Assistive tech can interpret the grid as single-select, which miscommunicates selection behavior to users. The root grid attributes should advertise multi-select whenever `selection_mode` is `Multiple`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTElh ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1825
parent: 3269730143
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve row index semantics in row link attrs**

`row_link_attrs` always delegates to `row_attrs`, which hardcodes `row_index = 0`. In virtual-scrolling mode this causes linked rows to report `aria-rowindex="1"` regardless of their actual position, so screen readers get incorrect row-position announcements. The link-attrs path needs an indexed variant or a row-index parameter.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "old_string": "/// Returns `true` when deselecting `key` would leave the selection empty.\nfn would_empty_after_deselect(set: &selection::Set, key: &Key) -> bool {\n    match set {\n        selection::Set::Single(k) => k == key,\n\n        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => keys.len() == 1 && keys.contains(key),\n\n        // `Empty` / `All` / unknown non-exhaustive variants are not at\n        // risk of becoming empty from a single deselect.\n        _ => false,\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Returns `true` when deselecting `key` would leave the selection empty.\nfn would_empty_after_deselect(set: &selection::Set, key: &Key) -> bool {\n    match set {\n        selection::Set::Single(k) => k == key,\n\n        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => keys.len() == 1 && keys.contains(key),\n\n        // `Empty` / `All` / unknown non-exhaustive variants are not at\n        // risk of becoming empty from a single deselect.\n        _ => false,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Walks `all_row_ids` starting from `current` (exclusive) in the\n/// indicated direction (`forward = true` for next, `false` for\n/// previous) and returns the first non-disabled row key. Returns `None`\n/// when no enabled row exists in that direction.\nfn next_enabled_row(\n    all_row_ids: &[&Key],\n    current: usize,\n    disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>,\n    forward: bool,\n) -> Option<Key> {\n    next_enabled_row_index(all_row_ids, current, disabled, forward).map(|i| all_row_ids[i].clone())\n}\n\n/// Index-returning variant of [`next_enabled_row`], used by\n/// `on_cell_keydown` which also needs the index to populate\n/// `Event::FocusCell::row_index`.\nfn next_enabled_row_index(\n    all_row_ids: &[&Key],\n    current: usize,\n    disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>,\n    forward: bool,\n) -> Option<usize> {\n    if forward {\n        ((current + 1)..all_row_ids.len()).find(|&i| !disabled.contains(all_row_ids[i]))\n    } else {\n        (0..current).rev().find(|&i| !disabled.contains(all_row_ids[i]))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Returns the first or last enabled row key. `from_start = true` walks\n/// forward from index 0; `false` walks backward from the end (for\n/// `End` / `Ctrl+End`). Returns `None` when every row is disabled.\nfn first_enabled_row(\n    all_row_ids: &[&Key],\n    disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>,\n    from_start: bool,\n) -> Option<Key> {\n    first_enabled_row_index(all_row_ids, disabled, from_start).map(|i| all_row_ids[i].clone())\n}\n\n/// Index variant of [`first_enabled_row`].\nfn first_enabled_row_index(\n    all_row_ids: &[&Key],\n    disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>,\n    from_start: bool,\n) -> Option<usize> {\n    if from_start {\n        (0..all_row_ids.len()).find(|&i| !disabled.contains(all_row_ids[i]))\n    } else {\n        (0..all_row_ids.len()).rev().find(|&i| !disabled.contains(all_row_ids[i]))\n    }\n}"
}
