That\n  silent downgrade dropped every unloaded row from selection on the\n  first individual deselect, which is a correctness break for\n  paginated tables. The agnostic core now keeps `Set::All` as the\n  global semantic and rejects the individual deselect — adapters\n  using AllData track exclusions via §5.2 `BulkSelection`.\n  `AllVisible` mode still materializes (which is correct because\n  `Set::All` there represents only the registered rows).\n\nP2 fixes:\n- `on_row_keydown` arrow / Home / End navigation now skips disabled\n  rows via a new `next_enabled_row` / `first_enabled_row` helper pair.\n  Previously focus could land on `aria-disabled` rows, which broke\n  the disabled-row contract for adapters.\n- `on_cell_keydown` ArrowUp / ArrowDown / Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End uses\n  the index-returning variant `next_enabled_row_index` /\n  `first_enabled_row_index` so the emitted `FocusCell::row_index`\n  matches the resolved row.\n- `table_attrs` now emits `aria-multiselectable=\"true\"` on the\n  interactive grid when `selection_mode == Multiple`, so assistive\n  tech doesn't read multi-select grids as single-select.\n- New `row_link_attrs_indexed(row_id, href, row_index)` API method.\n  `row_link_attrs` is retained as a non-virtualized convenience that\n  delegates with `row_index = 0`. Virtualized callers MUST use the\n  indexed variant so `aria-rowindex` reflects the row's actual\n  position in the dataset.\n\nThe two pass-1 `codex_*_materializes_set_all_for_individual_deselect`\ntests have been superseded — they were testing a behavior the new\ncontract forbids. Their replacements\n`codex_round4_{deselect,toggle}_row_keeps_set_all_in_all_data_mode`\nlock in the corrected behavior. The `materialize_all_against_rows`\nhelper is retained for the edge case where `Set::All` enters\n`AllVisible` selection via a controlled Bindable that subsequently\nexits controlled mode.\n\nTests: +10 new regression guards (TDD red → green) covering every\nfinding plus disabled-row edge cases (Home/End/no-enabled-successor).\nCoverage on the table file stays well above the 90% threshold at\n90.43% line / 90.38% branch.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-clamp cached widths when min_column_width changes**

When `Props::min_column_width` is updated through `set_props`, `SyncProps` updates `ctx.min_column_width` but leaves existing `ctx.column_widths` entries untouched. This allows previously resized columns to remain below the new minimum (e.g., width 60, new min 100), so subsequent `column_resize_handle_attrs` and adapter width application can expose values that violate the active constraint until the user resizes again.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTd56 ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1062
parent: 3269876637
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep disabled rows out of AllData select-all state**

In `SelectAllMode::AllData`, `Event::SelectAll` always writes `selection::Set::All`, which makes `is_row_selected` report `true` for disabled rows because `Set::All::contains` is unconditional. As a result, disabled rows can be surfaced as selected after select-all, contradicting the component contract that disabled rows are non-selectable and causing incorrect checkbox/row selection state in this mode.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTd5_ ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1734
parent: 3269876644
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude disabled rows from all-selected derivation**

`all_selected` checks every key in `all_row_ids` without filtering `ctx.disabled_keys`, even though `Event::SelectAll` intentionally skips disabled rows. In a multiple-select table with visible disabled rows, selecting all selectable rows still yields `aria-checked="mixed"` instead of `"true"`, so the header checkbox state is wrong despite the selection being complete for all selectable rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTd6B ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1231
parent: 3269876646
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebase focused_cell when SetRows runs without focused_row**

`SetRows` only rebases or clears focus when `ctx.focused_row` is set, but `Event::Focus` populates only `focused_cell`. If adapters use `Focus` (cell-index focus) and rows are reordered/removed, `focused_cell` can become stale or out-of-range, leaving no rendered cell with `tabindex="0"` and breaking roving-focus continuity after data updates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTd6C ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:2442
parent: 3269876648
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve non-sortable headers in part_attrs dispatch**

`ConnectApi::part_attrs` hardcodes `sortable=true` for `Part::ColumnHeader`, so callers using the generic dispatcher will always get sortable semantics (`aria-sort`, `tabindex=0`, `data-ars-sort`) even for non-sortable columns. This diverges from `column_header_attrs(..., sortable)` and can make static headers incorrectly focusable/sortable in adapters that rely on `part_attrs` wiring.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DTd6E ───
file: spec/components/data-display/table.md:88
parent: 3269876650
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fix SyncControlledSortDescriptor payload type in spec**

The event table documents `SyncControlledSortDescriptor` as `Option<SortDescriptor<String>>`, but the implemented event payload is `Option<Option<SortDescriptor<String>>>` so controlled mode can be entered/updated and exited. Following the current spec signature loses the controlled-mode toggle (`None` vs `Some(None)`) and will mislead adapter implementations about how to leave controlled sort mode.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    /// Returns `true` when every selectable key in `all_row_ids` is\n    /// currently selected. Disabled rows are excluded from the check\n    /// because they are non-selectable — selecting every selectable\n    /// row should yield `aria-checked=\"true\"` on the header checkbox,\n    /// not `\"mixed\"`. Handles [`selection::Set::All`] efficiently.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn all_selected(&self, all_row_ids: &[&Key]) -> bool {\n        let sel = self.ctx.selected_rows.get();\n\n        if sel.is_all() {\n            return true;\n        }\n\n        let selectable: Vec<&&Key> = all_row_ids\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|id| !self.ctx.disabled_keys.contains(**id))\n            .collect();\n\n        if selectable.is_empty() {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        selectable.iter().all(|id| sel.contains(**id))\n    }\n\n    /// Returns `true` when at least one selectable key in `all_row_ids`\n    /// is currently selected. Mirrors `all_selected`'s disabled-row\n    /// filter so the header checkbox's mixed/checked transitions\n    /// reflect \"some selectable rows are selected\".\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn some_selected(&self, all_row_ids: &[&Key]) -> bool {\n        let sel = self.ctx.selected_rows.get();\n\n        if sel.is_all() {\n            return all_row_ids\n                .iter()\n                .any(|id| !self.ctx.disabled_keys.contains(*id));\n        }\n\n        all_row_ids\n            .iter()\n            .any(|id| !self.ctx.disabled_keys.contains(*id) && sel.contains(*id))\n    }"
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve `Direction::Auto` before dispatching SetDirection**

When props change, `on_props_changed` forwards `new.dir` directly into `Event::SetDirection`, which means a transition like `Ltr -> Auto` stores `Auto` in `Context::dir` instead of a concrete direction. Keyboard handlers treat anything other than `Rtl` as LTR, so in RTL locales this can flip ArrowLeft/ArrowRight behavior until the adapter sends an extra corrective event. Resolve `Auto` to a concrete direction (or skip emitting `SetDirection` for `Auto`) in this path to keep directional keyboard navigation correct after prop updates.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Codex review pass 6 (PR #651) — Direction::Auto resolution in\n//      SetDirection transition.\n// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[test]\nfn codex_round6_set_direction_resolves_auto_from_locale() {\n    // Codex P2 (thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DT49S).\n    // `SetDirection(Direction::Auto)` must resolve `Auto` to a concrete\n    // direction via the active locale rather than storing `Auto` in\n    // `Context::dir`. Keyboard handlers compare `ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl`\n    // and treat everything else (including `Auto`) as LTR, so leaving\n    // `Auto` in context silently breaks RTL navigation after prop\n    // updates.\n    let mut service = service_with_rows(\n        Props {\n            dir: Direction::Rtl,\n            ..test_props()\n        },\n        &[],\n    );\n    assert_eq!(service.context().dir, Direction::Rtl);\n\n    // Adapter / parent flips the prop back to `Auto` (asks the\n    // platform to re-resolve). The default locale is LTR, so the\n    // resolved value should be `Ltr` — NOT `Auto`.\n    drop(service.send(Event::SetDirection(Direction::Auto)));\n\n    assert_eq!(\n        service.context().dir,\n        Direction::Ltr,\n        \"SetDirection(Auto) must resolve to a concrete direction via ctx.locale\",\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn codex_round6_set_direction_auto_via_props_change() {\n    // Companion test — `on_props_changed` forwards `new.dir` through\n    // `Event::SetDirection`. > AGENT

Skill loaded. Now I have enough to answer.

**Yes, `TypedChildrenFn<C>` is viable** — and it's the right call for `ClientOnly`. The component re-runs the closure when the `mounted` signal flips, so preserving the concrete view type (instead of erasing to `AnyView`) gives you static optimization and avoids `AnyView`'s vtable cost on every re-render. The standard Leptos pattern is essentially:

```rust
#[component]
pub fn ClientOnly<Chil, Fb>(
    #[prop(optional, into)] fallback: Option<TypedChildrenFn<Fb>>,
    children: TypedChildrenFn<Chil>,
) -> impl IntoView
where
    Chil: IntoView + Send + 'static,
    Fb:   IntoView + Send + 'static,
```

**Tradeoffs:**
- **Win:** zero-cost view rendering, better type inference at the call site, no `AnyView` allocation per re-render.
- **Cost:** two type params (because `children` and `fallback` typically differ in shape — a placeholder skeleton vs. real content). Slot composition where the caller wants `Box<dyn>` semantics gets more awkward, but for `ClientOnly` the call site always has concrete views, so it's pure upside there.
- **Open question:** Leptos's `<Show fallback=...>` uses the same dual-`TypedChildrenFn` pattern internally — that's the precedent. The current spec uses `ChildrenFn` likely because it's the simpler signature, not because there's a technical reason to.

**Recommendation:** update the spec to `TypedChildrenFn<Chil>` + `Option<TypedChildrenFn<Fb>>`. Since the Leptos `ClientOnly` adapter isn't implemented yet (only the spec exists), this is a clean spec-only edit on a future PR — out of scope for the current Table PR #651.

Want me to make that spec edit now (separate from the Codex review loop), or hold it for when the `ClientOnly` adapter lands?

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize selection when switching to single-select mode**

When `SyncProps` updates `selection_mode`, it mutates `ctx.selection_mode`/`ctx.selection_state.mode` but never coerces the existing uncontrolled selection set to match the new mode. If a table currently has multiple selected rows and props change from `Mode::Multiple` to `Mode::Single` (or `Mode::None`), `ctx.selected_rows` can still hold multiple keys, so the API/attrs can continue reporting multiple selected rows until a later user event happens to rewrite selection. This leaves the component in an invalid mode/state combination immediately after a prop update.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DWPq0 ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:2528
parent: 3270909124
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid hardcoding zero width in resize-handle dispatcher**

The generic `ConnectApi::part_attrs` path for `ColumnResizeHandle` calls `column_resize_handle_attrs(column, 0.0)`, which emits `aria-valuenow="0"` whenever no cached width exists. Any renderer/test-harness path that relies on `part_attrs` therefore gets a bogus range value that does not reflect the actual column width, producing incorrect accessibility state and inconsistent behavior versus the typed API that accepts a real width.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

─── thread PRRT_kwDORp4enM6DWPq5 ───
file: crates/ars-components/src/data_display/table/mod.rs:1350
parent: 3270909129
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-finite widths in column resize transitions**

The resize clamp only checks `width < min`, so a `NaN` (or other non-finite value) passes through unchanged and is stored in `ctx.column_widths`. After that, `column_resize_handle_attrs` will serialize that value into `aria-valuenow` (e.g., `"NaN"`), which is not a valid numeric ARIA range value, and subsequent keyboard resize math will keep propagating the invalid value. Guarding `Event::ColumnResize` against non-finite inputs prevents this persistent broken state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebase Set::All when leaving AllData select-all mode**

`SyncProps` copies `select_all_mode` into context but never normalizes an existing uncontrolled `selected_rows = Set::All` when mode changes from `AllData` to `AllVisible` (or `None`). In that state, helper logic like `all_selected()` still treats selection as dataset-wide, which contradicts the AllVisible semantics the implementation enforces elsewhere (`SelectAll` in AllVisible intentionally avoids writing `Set::All`). This can leave stale, incorrect selection semantics after a prop-only mode switch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

685	/// Materializes [`selection::Set::All`] against the registered row set
686	/// so that `selection::State::deselect` (which is a no-op on `Set::All`)
687	/// can subsequently drop individual keys. Used by [`Event::ToggleRow`]
688	/// and [`Event::DeselectRow`] to keep individual-deselect workable after
689	/// a bulk select-all.
690	fn materialize_all_against_rows(state: &selection::State, rows: &[Key]) -> selection::State {
691	    if !matches!(state.selected_keys, selection::Set::All) {
692	        return state.clone();
693	    }
694	    let materialized: BTreeSet<Key> = rows
695	        .iter()
696	        .filter(|k| !state.is_disabled(k))
697	        .cloned()
698	        .collect();
699	    let new_keys = match materialized.len() {
700	        0 => selection::Set::Empty,
701	        1 => selection::Set::Single(materialized.into_iter().next().unwrap()),
702	        _ => selection::Set::Multiple(materialized),
703	    };
704	    selection::State {
705	        selected_keys: new_keys,
706	        ..state.clone()
707	    }

### Round 7 of Codex review — done

**4 findings** (1 P1 + 3 P2):

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
